item.title: While Trump Floats a Kim Meeting, North Korea Flaunts Its U.S.-Range Missiles
item.description: Kim Jong Un took his family to a new military museum, where drones and missiles underscore a push to advance his military.

item.title: Drone Attacks on Ships Sailing Near NATO Waters Present Fresh Test for the Alliance
item.description: European leaders, who have accused Russia of brazen assaults on their soil, contend with strikes on ships skirting their waters.

item.title: Kimberly-Clark, Kenvue Win Conditional EU Approval for $40 Billion Tie-Up
item.description: The European Commission—the EU’s executive arm—said that the sale fully addresses officials’ earlier concerns that the deal could hinder competition in tampon markets in Czechia, Estonia, and Slovakia.

item.title: Best High-Yield Savings Accounts of October 2026: Up to 5.00%
item.description: Beat average interest rates with one of these top high-yield savings accounts.

item.title: U.K. Spy Agency Confronts Escalating Hybrid War With Russia and Iran
item.description: The head of MI5 has painted a sobering picture of a range of threats now facing Britain and European allies.

item.title: Oil Prices Fall as Traders Weigh Middle East Risks, Russian Diesel Supplies
item.description: Oil prices pulled back after three consecutive sessions of gains, but further downside might be limited by escalating tensions in the Middle East, constraining flows from the Persian Gulf.

item.title: The Morning Risk Report: Trump’s Diesel Deal With Russia Faces Questions From Lawmakers on Legality
item.description: Plus: U.K. floats payments for fraud whistleblowers and Delta delays Saudi Arabia plans.

item.title: A Demographic Mirage May Be Distorting China’s Economic Ambitions
item.description: Plus, Beijing’s tepid recovery efforts, falling government bond yields and why China resists joining the developed world.

item.title: China’s Young People Are Losing Faith in the Promise of Hard Work
item.description: Plus, Trump says he is “looking at” firing Kimberly Guilfoyle, and Iran rallies its people for a return to fighting.

item.title: Iran Fortifying Nuclear Sites and Rallying Its People for Return to Fighting
item.description: The regime, convinced President Trump is ready to attack again, sees the preparations as a deterrent.

item.title: China’s Weakening Economy Is Creating a Lost Generation
item.description: Young people are watching their bright futures disappear as the country’s job losses pile up and the milestones of adulthood slip further away.

item.title: Chinese Cars Now Dominate Europe’s Biggest Auto Show
item.description: Two years ago, nine brands from China were at the event. This time, there were about 20.

item.title: Russia Pounds Ukrainian Energy Despite Trump’s Ceasefire Announcement
item.description: The Russian attacks, including on gas infrastructure, a power plant and a substation, come as the U.S. heaps pressure on Ukraine to stop striking Russian oil refineries.

item.title: Iran-Backed Militants Are Tightening the Screws on Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince
item.description: Mohammed bin Salman is now caught by an economy weakened by heavy spending and miscalculations of the Houthi threat.

item.title: Delta Delays Plans for Nonstop Service to Saudi Arabia
item.description: The carrier said it now expects to debut the flight in March, pushing back previous plans for an Oct. 23 rollout, after several fatal strikes at Riyadh’s international airport.

item.title: EU Aims to Put Brakes on Chinese Hybrid-Vehicle Market Share With Import Cap
item.description: The EU will restrict imports from the country to 350,000 units a year, with the aim of more-than halving China’s projected shipments to the bloc.

item.title: Xi’s Superpower Ambitions Fuel a Dangerous Debt Spiral in China
item.description: Chinese leader Xi Jinping is presiding over a dangerous spiral of debt that is strangling the economy at home and damaging trade partners around the world.

item.title: NATO’s Top Commander Lays Out Plan to Thwart a Russian Attack on the Alliance
item.description: Gen. Alexus Grynkewich outlined a series of steps to block an initial attack and break the adversary’s ability to control and support its forces.

item.title: The Morning Risk Report: Courts Grapple With Problem of People Betting on the Outcome of Jury Cases
item.description: Plus: The U.S. is sanctioning the International Criminal Court and AI has a God problem.

item.title: Trump’s Russian-Diesel Move Draws Pushback, Skepticism
item.description: Plus, retailers are spending tariff refunds on pre-holiday marketing, and China’s Geely is planning to sell EVs to Canadians next year.
